payload.task_text:
I need to review our product ratings and set up a feedback process for our underperforming products. Please look at all products in our store that have customer reviews and find the five products with the lowest average ratings. If there are ties in average rating, prefer products with more reviews.

For these five lowest-rated products, create a Google Form titled Product Quality Improvement Survey with a description explaining that we are gathering customer feedback to improve product quality. For each of the five products, add a required rating question asking customers to rate their overall satisfaction with that product on a scale of one to five, using the product name in the question text. Implement each rating question as a single-choice (multiple choice) question whose options are the five values 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and set it as required. Also add one optional text question at the end asking for additional suggestions for improvement.

Create an Excel file called Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx with a sheet called Review Summary that lists all reviewed products, one row per product, with columns for Product_Name truncated to sixty characters, Avg_Rating rounded to two decimal places, Review_Count, and Category using the first category name from each product. Sort by Avg_Rating in ascending order. Add a second sheet called Stats with Metric and Value rows for Total_Products_Reviewed, Lowest_Rated_Product with the product name truncated to forty characters, and Avg_Rating_Overall as the average rating across all reviewed products rounded to two decimal places. Write all numeric values (Avg_Rating, Review_Count, Total_Products_Reviewed, Avg_Rating_Overall) as literal numbers, not spreadsheet formulas.

Schedule a product quality review meeting in the calendar on March 20 2026 from 2pm to 3pm with the title Product Quality Review Meeting.

Send an email to product.team@company.com with subject Product Quality Alert - Review Required mentioning the names of the five lowest-rated products and requesting the team to review them.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use one read-only Explore wave for the 82-product/396-review store join, then one writer wave with two parallel coder sub-agents. No plan agent is used: the frozen payload between the waves is the complete plan.

Dynamically resolve the workspace and freeze the ranking contract: every product with at least one review, ranked by average rating ascending, review count descending, then stable Product_ID; the five lowest define the survey, meeting and email. Start the fixed-date event inventory independently.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 1 Explore sub-agent (read-only):

   1. explore 0 (enterprise-data-analyst 0): Review gatherer: paginate both store endpoints with perPage=100 and increasing page until a short or empty page, omitting review status and preserving observed statuses. Join strictly on Product_ID; for every product with at least one review compute the literal Review_Count and the average rating (full precision, 2-decimal display), keeping the full product name and the first category. Select the lowest five by average rating ascending, review count descending, then stable Product_ID. Return only the complete reviewed-products table (id, full name, avg_rating, review_count, first category), the frozen five-row ranking with complete product names, record counts, duplicate IDs, and page controls — no writes, no full item arrays.

After Wave 1, verify the handoff in one single pass: row count equals the product join, every reviewed product covered, five-row ranking unambiguous. The main agent then freezes one canonical product_review_data.json in the workspace containing: the products list (82 objects with id, full name, avg_rating 2 decimals, review_count, category), the frozen bottom-five ranking with complete names, and the Stats values (Total_Products_Reviewed, Lowest_Rated_Product truncated to forty characters, Avg_Rating_Overall rounded to two decimals). This file is the single binding input for Wave 2; nobody re-reads the store afterwards.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 2 coder sub-agents in parallel, both consuming product_review_data.json verbatim with no recomputation and no store reads:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Workbook writer — sole writer of Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx. Create it exactly once with exactly two sheets: Review Summary with columns Product_Name (truncated to sixty characters), Avg_Rating (two decimals), Review_Count, Category (first category), one row per reviewed product sorted by Avg_Rating ascending; Stats with columns Metric, Value and rows Total_Products_Reviewed, Lowest_Rated_Product (truncated to forty characters), Avg_Rating_Overall (two decimals). Write all numeric values as literal numbers, never formulas; read both populated ranges back and return path, sheet order, row counts and equality controls.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 0): External writer — sole owner of form, event and email. Forms has no list/search: call create_form exactly once titled Product Quality Improvement Survey with the stated description, never retry an ambiguous failure, then append sequentially on that one formId five add_multiple_choice_question calls in frozen rank order, each using the product name in the question text with options ["1","2","3","4","5"] and required=true, followed by one add_text_question(..., required=false) for additional suggestions; call get_form and verify title/description/question order/types/options/flags. Filter list_events(timeMin="2026-03-20T00:00:00", timeMax="2026-03-21T00:00:00", maxResults=100, orderBy="startTime") locally for the exact Product Quality Review Meeting at 14:00-15:00; create it once only if missing with exact start.dateTime/end.dateTime, retain the ID, and call get_event. Paginate Sent search for product.team@company.com and exact subject Product Quality Alert - Review Required, send at most once naming the frozen five products, then read it back.

After Wave 2, verify both handoffs in one single pass against product_review_data.json: workbook cell-for-cell, five-question form structure, event identity, and email contents. Accept only after every read-back matches the frozen payload, then call claim_done. Do not dispatch any further agent after Wave 2.

nodes.text:
You are a read-only data gatherer for a WooCommerce product review analysis. Do NOT write any files, do NOT create/update/delete anything, do NOT call any non-read tools. Goal: produce the complete reviewed-products dataset and freeze the bottom-five ranking.

Environment: A WooCommerce store is accessible via the mcp__woocommerce__* tools (read/list/get only).

Tasks:
1. Products: Paginate mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_list with perPage=100 and page=1, 2, 3, ... until a page returns fewer than 100 items or an empty list. For each product record keep: id, name (exact, full), and the FIRST category name from its categories array (use empty string if categories is empty or absent).
2. Reviews: Paginate mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_reviews_list WITHOUT passing the status parameter (so all statuses are preserved as observed). Use perPage=100 and page=1,2,... until a short or empty page. Note the set of review statuses you observed. For each review keep the product id it belongs to (use the numeric product id, whether the field is named product, product_id, or similar) and its rating.
3. Join strictly on product id. For every product having at least one review: Review_Count = exact number of reviews; Avg_Rating = mean of its review ratings computed at FULL precision (keep e.g. 4+ decimals); also compute a 2-decimal display value (standard round-half-up). Keep the full product name and first category.
4. Rank every reviewed product by Avg_Rating ascending (full precision), then Review_Count descending, then product id ascending as the final stable tiebreak. The bottom five rows are the frozen five lowest-rated products (rank 1 = lowest).
5. Compute Avg_Rating_Overall = mean of the per-product Avg_Rating values across ALL reviewed products (full precision), rounded to 2 decimals for display. Total_Products_Reviewed = number of products with at least one review.

Report back (text only, exhaustive — do not truncate):
- Counts: total products fetched, total reviews fetched, number of reviewed products, number of unreviewed products; pages used for each endpoint; any duplicate product ids or duplicate review ids; observed review statuses.
- The COMPLETE reviewed-products table, one row per reviewed product, in the ranked order (lowest avg first), with columns: product_id | full product name | avg_rating (full precision) | avg_rating_display (2 decimals) | review_count | first_category. Include EVERY reviewed product.
- The frozen bottom-five ranking: rank | product_id | full product name | avg_rating (full precision) | review_count | first_category, with a sentence of tie-break evidence for each of the five.
- Avg_Rating_Overall (full precision and 2-decimal display) and Total_Products_Reviewed.
Gather product review data

Continue your previous read-only data-gathering task. Your prior report truncated many product names with "..." (e.g., product 21 ended "...Gen...", product 1 ended "...Acti...", product 5 "...Wal..."). The canonical payload downstream requires FULL, EXACT, untruncated product names for all products, especially the bottom five.

Please output, with ABSOLUTELY NO truncation of any name:
1. The complete exact product name for ALL 82 products as compact JSON lines: [id, "full exact name"] — one per line, ids 1..82. Use the exact name strings from the store (you may re-read the product list read-only if needed, e.g., via mcp__woocommerce__woo_products_list with perPage=20 and pages 1-5, or any read tool that returns full records).
2. The five frozen bottom-five product ids (61, 21, 46, 76, 25) with their full exact names verbatim, one per line, and confirm each name is complete (no trailing "...", no ellipsis).

If the full list is too large for a single response, split it across multiple parts and clearly label Part 1, Part 2, ... Do not write any files, do not modify anything. Read-only only.
Complete full product names

You are the SOLE writer of an Excel workbook (office-report-builder). Do NOT touch the store (no WooCommerce calls), do NOT recompute anything — the canonical data file is authoritative.

INPUT FILE (read it with mcp__local__python_execute using json.load, or any available local read tool):
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-wc-product-review-analysis-gform-gcal/workspace/product_review_data.json

Its structure: meta (counts), products = list of 82 objects in ranked order (lowest avg first) with fields: id, name (full), avg_rating (numeric, 2 decimals), avg_rating_full, review_count (int), category, name_60 (pre-truncated to 60 chars). bottom_five = 5 objects with rank, name, name_40. stats = {Total_Products_Reviewed: 82, Lowest_Rated_Product: name truncated to 40 chars, Avg_Rating_Overall: 4.62}.

OUTPUT FILE: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-wc-product-review-analysis-gform-gcal/workspace/Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx
Create it with mcp__excel__* tools. It must contain EXACTLY TWO sheets in this order:

Sheet 1 named "Review Summary":
- Row 1 header: Product_Name | Avg_Rating | Review_Count | Category
- One row per product from file["products"] in the given order (already sorted by Avg_Rating ascending). Product_Name = file value name_60 (already truncated to 60 chars). Avg_Rating = the literal numeric 2-decimal value (e.g. 3.71) — a NUMBER, never a formula string. Review_Count = literal integer. Category = the category string (may be empty string).
- Total rows = 83 (1 header + 82 products).

Sheet 2 named "Stats":
- Row 1 header: Metric | Value
- Row 2: Total_Products_Reviewed | 82 (literal number)
- Row 3: Lowest_Rated_Product | file["stats"]["Lowest_Rated_Product"] (string, already truncated to 40 chars)
- Row 4: Avg_Rating_Overall | 4.62 (literal number)

Rules:
- All numeric values (Avg_Rating, Review_Count, Total_Products_Reviewed, Avg_Rating_Overall) MUST be literal numbers, NOT spreadsheet formulas (no leading "="), NOT text strings.
- Handle the default sheet created by create_workbook: rename it to "Review Summary" (or create "Review Summary" and delete the default), then create "Stats". Sheet order must be Review Summary first, Stats second. Ensure no extra sheets remain.
- Optional: apply number format "0.00" to the Avg_Rating column and the Value column for display; do NOT change the values.

VERIFY (mandatory): after writing, call mcp__excel__get_workbook_metadata (confirm sheet names and order, only 2 sheets) and mcp__excel__read_data_from_excel on both sheets over the full populated range. Check: header text exact; Review Summary has 83 rows; every Product_Name equals the JSON name_60; every Avg_Rating equals the JSON avg_rating number; every Review_Count equals JSON review_count; every Category matches; Stats has 4 rows with the 3 expected Metric/Value pairs; none of the numeric cells contain a formula (no value starting with "=") and none are strings.

RETURN: absolute file path; sheet order; Review Summary row count; Stats row count; a statement that all numeric cells are literal numbers (not formulas); confirmation every cell matched the JSON payload; or a precise list of any mismatches. Do not write any other files.
Build Product_Review_Analysis.xlsx

You are the SOLE owner of external workflow side effects (external-workflow-operator): a Google Form, a Google Calendar event, and an email. Do NOT touch the store (no WooCommerce calls), do NOT recompute anything.

INPUT FILE (read it with mcp__local__python_execute using json.load, or any available local read tool):
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-wc-product-review-analysis-gform-gcal/workspace/product_review_data.json

file["bottom_five"] = 5 objects in frozen rank order (rank 1 = LOWEST-rated product): {rank, id, name (FULL product name as stored), avg_rating, review_count, category}.

=== 1. GOOGLE FORM (mcp__google_forms__*) ===
- Call create_form EXACTLY ONCE: title = "Product Quality Improvement Survey", description = a clear description stating that we are gathering customer feedback to improve product quality (e.g. "We are gathering customer feedback to improve the quality of our products. Your responses will help us identify and fix issues."). Keep the returned formId; never retry a failure ambiguously.
- On that SAME formId, in frozen rank order (rank 1 first, then 2, 3, 4, 5), call add_multiple_choice_question FIVE times — once per product — with:
    questionTitle = "Rate your overall satisfaction with {FULL product name} on a scale of one to five" (use the exact full product name from the JSON),
    options = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5"],
    required = true.
- Then call add_text_question ONCE on the same formId, required = false, questionTitle = something like "Please share any additional suggestions for improvement".
- Call get_form and verify: title == "Product Quality Improvement Survey"; description mentions gathering customer feedback to improve product quality; exactly 6 questions; questions 1-5 are single-choice/multiple-choice (radio) with options exactly 1,2,3,4,5 and required=true, each containing its product name; question 6 is a text question with required=false.

=== 2. GOOGLE CALENDAR (mcp__google_calendar__*) ===
- Call list_events(timeMin="2026-03-20T00:00:00", timeMax="2026-03-21T00:00:00", maxResults=100, orderBy="startTime"). Filter locally for an event titled EXACTLY "Product Quality Review Meeting" with start 2026-03-20T14:00:00 and end 2026-03-20T15:00:00.
- If exactly one such event exists, reuse its eventId (do NOT create a duplicate).
- If none exists, call create_event ONCE: summary = "Product Quality Review Meeting", start = {"dateTime": "2026-03-20T14:00:00"}, end = {"dateTime": "2026-03-20T15:00:00"}. Keep the returned eventId.
- Call get_event(eventId) and confirm summary/start/end match.

=== 3. EMAIL (mcp__emails__*) ===
- BEFORE sending, check whether an identical email already exists: search_emails(query="Product Quality Alert - Review Required", folder="Sent", page_size=50) and inspect results for a message to product.team@company.com with that exact subject. If one exists, do NOT send again — report it.
- Otherwise send EXACTLY ONCE: to = "product.team@company.com", subject = "Product Quality Alert - Review Required", body = a professional message that (a) names all five lowest-rated products (list their FULL names, rank 1 = lowest, from the JSON bottom_five) and (b) requests the team to review these five products (e.g. please review these products and take action to improve quality).
- Read it back: search_emails in Sent for the subject, confirm recipient product.team@company.com, subject exact, and that all five full product names appear in the body.

RETURN: formId + form verification details (title, description, question order/types/options/required flags); eventId + confirmed start/end; email result (sent or already existed) + read-back confirmation (recipient, subject, all five product names present); and any mismatch found. Do not write any files.
Create form, event, and email
